jobs.title: Category Manager Asian & Tribal Arts
jobs.description:
At Catawiki, every day brings the extraordinary! Whether it’s Daniel Ricciardo’s Formula 1 Car , a Woolly Mammoth’s Skeleton , Lady Gaga's Jumpsuit or Usain Bolt’s running shoe , we encounter exceptional objects every day.

We’re a one-of-a-kind marketplace for buying and selling special objects. Each week, more than 100,000 unique items are auctioned, all carefully curated by our passionate in-house experts.

Having sold over 25 million unique objects, our mission is to become the world’s most popular destination for special objects. As a growing, diverse and sustainable scale-up, we proudly live by three core values. If these values resonate with you, we’d love to explore how you can join us.

- Taking ownership and driving impact

- Being open to change and feedback

- Being passionate about our mission and our customers.

About the role

Asian & Tribal Art is one of Catawiki’s most distinctive and commercially complex categories. It brings together Asian Art, Tribal and Ethnographic Art, where expertise, provenance and collector trust matter.

This is a commercial marketplace leadership role, not a traditional FMCG or buying role.

As Category Manager, you will build and own the category’s end-to-end supply and demand strategy. You will grow high-quality + young collector orientated supply, shape the buyer and auction proposition, own commercial performance and directly lead an international expert team.

What you’ll do

- Build and own the end-to-end marketplace strategy, growing high-quality supply and creating demand from serious buyers and collectors

- Own the category P&L and use data to make clear decisions on supply, demand, pricing, reserve-price strategy and performance

- Shape auction and demand planning around seasonality, collector behaviour, market movements and seller portfolios

- Build long-term relationships with high-quality sellers and serious buyers, working closely with Sales and Business Development

- Directly manage, coach and develop the expert team, including performance, talent development and succession planning

- Work cross-functionally with Marketing, Operations, Product and Commercial teams to unlock growth and improve the buyer experience

What you’ll bring

- Marketplace, e-commerce, category or commercial leadership experience in a similarly complex business

- A track record of owning growth, budgets or P&L outcomes and turning plans into results

- A data-driven, action-oriented approach and the confidence to make decisions quickly

- Proven direct people-management experience, including coaching, performance management, talent development and succession planning

- Strong influencing and communication skills across teams, stakeholders, sellers and buyers

- Entrepreneurial energy, resilience and a hands-on approach in a fast-moving environment

You do not need to be an Asian & Tribal Art specialist. What matters most is your commercial leadership, ability to build trust and ambition to grow a category with real depth and potential.

What success looks like

- A clear end-to-end marketplace strategy is in motion, with priorities, owners and measurable outcomes

- A strong pipeline of not only high-quality, repeat sellers and buyers but also spotting new supply opportunities and how to reach a young collector audience

- More consistent auction quality, commercial discipline and buyer experience

- An engaged, motivated and self sufficient expert team with a growth mindset, personal development ambitions and commercial mindset

Why You'll Love Working with Us

- Create a visible impact by working at scale in a global organisation serving millions of customers across 80+ categories. In our flat structure, every role has a broad scope and directly impacts both our customers and the business.

- Learn and grow through our Learning & Development initiatives, including clear development plans and mentorship programmes to support your career progression.

- A culture of connection defines us . We’re a passionate, diverse team of 800+ Catawikians representing 60+ nationalities. We foster an inclusive and queer-friendly environment where everyone is encouraged to bring their full self to work.

- Celebrate life’s moments with us. You’ll receive a €100 Catavoucher when you join, a €50 Catavoucher on your birthday, and an extra day off each year to “Pursue Your Passion ” . We also offer additional leave for key work anniversaries and important life events. Benefits may vary by location.

Our Offices and Way of Working

Our vibrant offices in Amsterdam and Lisbon are designed to inspire collaboration. Most Catawikians operate in a hybrid setup, combining office-based and remote work, with a minimum of two days per week in the office, unless a role is explicitly stated as fully remote or fully office-based.

Interested?

Apply with an English CV and Cover Letter. By applying, you agree to Catawiki’s Applicant Privacy Policy. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every requirement, we still encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

About the role

Special objects are the final frontier of e-commerce. As Senior Category Lead for Art – Primary Market, you’ll bring structure and consistency to the team’s day-to-day work. You’ll turn priorities into clear plans, strengthen how work moves across the team, and help each person take ownership of outcomes. Alongside this operational focus, you’ll support the Senior Category Manager in translating the category vision into practical initiatives that improve the experience for buyers and sellers.

You’ll create an engaged team culture built on trust, clear expectations, and accountability, helping people build on their strengths and grow in their roles.

You’ll also coordinate with Sales, Marketing, and other relevant teams to deliver cross-functional improvements and keep the category’s priorities moving.

What you’ll do

- Create a clear operating rhythm: Turn category priorities into practical plans with clear owners, milestones, and regular follow-up so work moves forward reliably.

- Improve day-to-day operations: Clarify workflows and handovers, spot bottlenecks early, and help the team resolve blockers.

- Build team ownership and accountability: Set clear goals and expectations, coach team members to take responsibility for their work, and help them use their strengths.

- Strengthen engagement and development: Hold regular 1:1s, give timely feedback, and support each person’s growth in partnership with the Senior Category Manager.

- Use performance insights to guide action: Monitor category results, identify risks and opportunities, and coordinate focused actions with relevant teams.

- Translate strategy into delivery: Support the Senior Category Manager’s vision by coordinating cross-functional initiatives from planning through execution and review.

- Identify category growth opportunities: Use market and performance insight to spot where the category can grow, then work with relevant teams to turn promising opportunities into practical initiatives.

What you’ll bring

- Operational leadership: You have a strong track record of creating structure, setting priorities, and ensuring reliable execution in a category, sales, or commercial team.

- Team leadership and coaching: You help colleagues perform at their best through clear goals, regular feedback, coaching, and support.

- Ownership and accountability: You set clear expectations, follow through on commitments, and encourage others to take responsibility for outcomes.

- Organised project delivery: You coordinate cross-functional work, manage dependencies and timelines, and keep stakeholders aligned.

- Analytical judgment: You use data and customer or market insight to identify issues, set priorities, and evaluate results.

- Clear, constructive communication: You build trust, share context, give direct feedback, and adapt your communication to different stakeholders.

- Interest in contemporary art: You bring a genuine interest in contemporary art and the primary art market.

How we work in the Art Team

- We’re a supportive, friendly Art team that works together to tackle ambitious growth challenges.

- You’ll work across Art – Primary Market , supporting the Direct from the Artist and Photography categories with clear day-to-day priorities and coordinated delivery.

- You’ll collaborate with Sales, Marketing, HR, and relevant partner teams , agreeing owners and next steps so decisions turn into action.

What You’ll Do

- Define and own the strategic roadmap for People Operations, payroll, well-being and facilities, aligned with the Business and People strategy.

What You’ll Bring

- Bring 12+ years of relevant experience in an international, fast-growing organisation, with deep expertise in People Operations and experience in areas such as Reward, Employee Relations, well-being or Facilities.

- Demonstrate experience leading multi-country People Operations at scale, including payroll, benefits, compensation operations, compliance and process improvement.

- Apply strong knowledge of employment law and employee relations practices in the Netherlands and other European countries, with sound judgement on complex cases and when to involve legal specialists.

- Bring experience with reward and benefits programmes inside and outside the Netherlands, including role and salary benchmarking.

- Use data, automation and emerging technologies, including AI, to challenge existing processes, improve decision-making and build scalable ways of working.

- Translate strategy into practical execution while managing priorities effectively in a fast-paced, hybrid and international environment.

- Communicate effectively and build trusted relationships with employees, managers, senior leaders and external partners, with professional fluency in English; Dutch is a strong plus.

- Our People team of around 40 people, mainly based across Amsterdam and Lisbon, works collaboratively and openly, using data and AI to inform our thinking while staying closely connected to the needs of the business. We also make time to connect socially and enjoy working together.

- Our senior leaders combine strategic direction with hands-on operational execution, with a focus on clear ownership, speed and scalable foundations.

- Our People team use data, insights and employee feedback to identify risks and opportunities and turn them into practical improvements.
